claim_boundary: Sources support bounded design rationales. They do not validate ChildEsc scenario wording, labels, target sets, realism, prevalence, or deployment safety.

sources.title: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Child Safety in AI
supports: synthetic evaluation under restricted-access conditions
privacy-preserving auditing
deployment safeguards
child-centered design and external-stakeholder collaboration
sources.does_not_support: Any empirical ChildEsc label or safety-effectiveness claim.

sources.title: Preventing AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material Necessitates New Approaches to AI Safety
supports: transparent and reproducible standardized safety assessments
robustness and independence as evaluation requirements
limits of static benchmarks
sources.does_not_support: A claim that ChildEsc evaluates AIG-CSAM capability; B3 is only an assessment-method analogy.

sources.title: Beyond 'I Can't Help With That': How Child Safety Experts Evaluate AI Chatbot Safety
supports: binary refusal is insufficient in vulnerable child interactions
context gathering and tailored human support are important
a parent or caregiver cannot be assumed safe
sources.does_not_support: ChildEsc target taxonomy completeness or item-level labels.

sources.title: Guidance on AI and Children 3.0
supports: child rights, agency, privacy, inclusion, and age-appropriate design
participatory and stakeholder-informed development
sources.does_not_support: A clinical routing threshold or a universal handoff preference.

sources.title: When AI Becomes a Friend: Child Rights Risks, Harms, and Regulatory Responses to AI Chatbots and Companions
supports: avoidance of exclusivity, dependency, and emotional primacy
crisis protocols and context-specific referral pathways
high-risk detection, internal escalation, privacy, and near-miss monitoring
sources.does_not_support: That a lexical dependency cue is sufficient for a particular ChildEsc action.

sources.title: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline Best Practices
supports: active collaboration with a person at risk
least-invasive intervention
involuntary emergency intervention only as a last resort
sources.does_not_support: Automated crisis classification, emergency contact, or child-specific clinical labels.

sources.title: Collecting, Using, or Sharing Consumer Health Information?
supports: affirmative express consent where appropriate
clear and conspicuous health-data disclosures
purpose limitation, retention limits, access controls, and auditability
sources.does_not_support: Treating a bundled terms-of-service clause as legally or ethically sufficient authorization for crisis-data disclosure.

sources.title: The Age of Curiosity Meets the Age of AI: Benchmarking Child Safety in Large Language Models
supports: controlled explicit and implicit child-context conditions
age-scoped wording
multi-turn, cross-lingual, and cultural evaluation as separate dimensions
sources.does_not_support: ChildEsc action labels or a claim that its English synthetic language is realistic.

sources.title: CAREBench: A Child-Safety Risk Benchmark for Language Models
supports: upstream child-risk categories
responsibly scoped prompts without explicit abuse material
recognize, refuse, de-escalate, and redirect behavior
sources.does_not_support: Novelty of crisis referral or redirection in ChildEsc.

sources.title: CARE-Bench: Benchmarking Patient-Facing LLM Triage
supports: controlled information-state prefixes
source-to-case transformation rationales
ordered action errors and timing thresholds
separate development, validation, public-test, and controlled-access splits
sources.does_not_support: Novelty of four-label action timing in ChildEsc or transfer of medical triage labels to child-safety handoff.

sources.title: MindEval: Benchmarking Language Models on Multi-turn Mental Health Support
supports: multi-turn evaluation
expert-designed rubrics
meta-evaluation of automated simulators and judges
sources.does_not_support: Using an unvalidated automated judge for ChildEsc or extrapolating adult therapy quality to children.

sources.title: A Scoping Review of Large Language Models for Generative Tasks in Mental Health Care
supports: priority of safety, privacy, and fairness
need for standardized constructs and transparent reporting
limits of ad hoc scales and simulated vignettes without clinical validation
sources.does_not_support: Clinical validity of ChildEsc's operational severity scale.

sources.title: Measuring What Matters: Construct Validity in Large Language Model Benchmarks
supports: precise construct definitions and claim chains
representativeness and contamination caveats
uncertainty, error analysis, and controlled sensitivity tests
sources.does_not_support: That documentation alone establishes construct validity.

sources.title: BetterBench: Assessing AI Benchmarks, Uncovering Issues, and Establishing Best Practices
supports: working evaluation code and reproducibility scripts
documentation of construction, assumptions, metrics, limitations, and release requirements
sources.does_not_support: Scientific validity based only on artifact completeness.
